scope: 对7个已有解释样板核对外部课程标准、统计教育框架、实证研究和技术定义，并落实与来源目标相关的解释修订。来源记录与内容修订不等于独立数学教研或儿童理解验收。

rules: 课程标准用于内容与年级目标对齐，不证明某种讲法有效。
实证研究保留样本、年龄、研究设计和限制，不把小样本结果泛化。
技术手册用于核对定义和图表约定，不当作儿童学习效果研究。
区分外部来源支持、数学事实核验、教学设计推断和本项目儿童测试。
源 taxonomy 的 hasResearch=false 保持原值；外部证据先独立登记，不伪装成已接入产品研究资料系统。

sourceCatalog.title: Australian Curriculum v9 — AC9M5ST03
sourceCatalog.supports: Year 5 plan and conduct investigations by posing questions, collecting relevant data, choosing displays, interpreting data and communicating findings in context; elaborations include objective, unbiased survey questions.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Curriculum expectation, not evidence that a particular teaching design is effective.

sourceCatalog.title: Pre-K–12 Guidelines for Assessment and Instruction in Statistics Education II (GAISE II)
sourceCatalog.supports: ASA Pre-K–12 framework: formulate questions, collect/consider data, analyze data and interpret results; defines mean absolute deviation as average distance from the mean and develops it at Level B.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Professional framework, not a controlled trial of each individual lesson or display.

sourceCatalog.title: Effects of an Inquiry-Oriented Curriculum and Professional Development Program on Grade 7 Students’ Understanding of Statistics and on Statistics Instruction
sourceCatalog.supports: 40 middle schools randomly assigned to an inquiry-oriented statistics unit plus four days of teacher professional development or usual practice; student statistics understanding improved by 0.23 SD (about 9 percentile points).
sourceCatalog.limitation: Curriculum and teacher development were bundled; one Florida district; no isolated effect for a single explanation field.

sourceCatalog.title: Attending to Middle School Students’ Understanding of Study Design: The Often Overlooked or Contrived Step in the Statistical Problem-Solving Process
sourceCatalog.authors: Sarai Hedges, Shelly Sheats Harkness and Kim Given
sourceCatalog.supports: Middle-school lesson study on nonexperimental study design; students intuitively used a naïve conception of stratified random sampling and recognized some forms of bias.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Lesson-based discourse analysis, not a universal effect-size estimate.

sourceCatalog.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics
sourceCatalog.supports: 6.SP.B.4 includes dot plots, histograms and box plots; 6.SP.B.5c includes mean absolute deviation; 6.G.A.1 covers polygon decomposition; 6.G.A.4 covers nets and surface area; 7.G.B.6 covers composite area, volume and surface area.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Defines expected content, not the best teaching method or proof of learning.

sourceCatalog.title: The Effects of 3D-Representation Instruction on Composite-Solid Surface-Area Learning for Elementary School Students
sourceCatalog.authors: Yao-Ting Sung, Pao-Chen Shih and Kuo-En Chang
sourceCatalog.supports: 111 fifth-grade students; a Google SketchUp-supported program (56 students) was compared with traditional instruction (55); the intervention group performed better on immediate and maintained achievement tests.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Specific software-supported intervention and grade-five sample; does not validate every prism formula or task.

sourceCatalog.title: Learning to calculate surface area: a focus on strategy choice
sourceCatalog.supports: Year 8 classroom intervention with 47 students aged 13–14 elicited multiple strategies and justifications for surface area of cubes and simple prisms.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Small classroom study on simple prisms; age range slightly above this node’s 12–13 range.

sourceCatalog.title: Dynamic Measurement Reasoning for Area and Volume
sourceCatalog.supports: Design experiments with fourth-grade students illustrate dynamic measurement reasoning for generating rectangles, right prisms and right cylinders.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Conceptual article and design experiments, not a controlled trial of this project’s tasks.

sourceCatalog.title: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook — Measures of Scale
sourceCatalog.supports: Defines average absolute deviation from the mean as AAD and median absolute deviation from the median as MAD; differs from school-statistics usage in GAISE II, where MAD means mean absolute deviation.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Acronym is convention-dependent; spell out mean absolute deviation when introducing this node.

sourceCatalog.title: School Students’ Understanding of Stacked Dot (or Line) Plots
sourceCatalog.authors: Jane M. Watson and Ben A. Kelly
sourceCatalog.supports: Students in Grades 5–10 compared stacked dot plots with usual number-line scaling and plots that omitted zero-value gaps.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Conference research paper with task-specific findings; not a universal teaching sequence.

sourceCatalog.title: NIST Dataplot — Strip Plot (also known as a dot plot)
sourceCatalog.supports: Defines dot/strip plots as observations along a value axis and explains stacking repeated values; notes typical use with small data sets.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Technical display definition, not age-specific teaching research.

sourceCatalog.title: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook — Histogram
sourceCatalog.supports: Defines common histograms using equal-sized bins and frequency counts; identifies center, spread, skewness, outliers and multiple modes.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Node covers equal-width frequency histograms, not unequal-width frequency-density histograms.

sourceCatalog.title: Students’ Understanding of Bar Graphs and Histograms: Results From the LOCUS Assessments
sourceCatalog.supports: LOCUS assessment responses from Grades 6–12 reveal misunderstandings in reading histograms and distinguishing them from bar graphs.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Broad grade range; findings should not be assumed to apply equally to every child aged 11–13.

sourceCatalog.title: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook — Box Plot
sourceCatalog.supports: Defines five-number-summary box plots with min/max whiskers and separately documents a fence-based variant using 1.5-IQR limits and outlier points.
sourceCatalog.limitation: More than one whisker convention is used; teaching materials must state which convention is shown.

sourceCatalog.title: Interpretations of Boxplots: Helping Middle School Students to Think Outside the Box
sourceCatalog.authors: Thomas G. Edwards, Aslı Özgün-Koca and John Barr
sourceCatalog.supports: Two-school study with 259 middle-school students found that students who could construct box plots could still struggle to interpret aggregated data and quartiles.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Two convenience-sampled schools; not a population-wide prevalence estimate.

sourceCatalog.title: Comparing Box Plot Distributions: A Teacher’s Reasoning
sourceCatalog.supports: Analyzes a Year 11 teacher’s reasoning when comparing box-plot distributions and develops a model of distinguishable reasoning elements, including sampling and reference context.
sourceCatalog.limitation: One teacher in a Year 11 class context; supplementary, not a direct age match.

sourceCatalog.title: Learning to measure the area of composite shapes
sourceCatalog.supports: Classroom design study in two Year 8 classes (31 participating students) documents decomposition, component-area measurement and recomposition strategies; discusses errors such as adding rather than subtracting outside pieces.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Small classroom design study; supports strategy development but does not prove every child will master it without instruction.

records.title: 规划统计调查
records.alignment: AC9M5ST03 directly aligns with posing an investigative question, collecting relevant data, selecting displays, interpreting results and communicating findings in context. GAISE II supplies the broader investigation cycle.
records.research: The IES STEPSS cluster-randomized study provides evidence for inquiry-oriented statistics instruction at Grade 7. Hedges et al. identify study design and data collection as a distinct reasoning challenge for middle-school students.
coverageAudit: Make the comparison question explicit: school-night versus weekend sleep duration.
Distinguish population, sample, variable, unit and collection method, including self-report and sample limitations.
Explain why a paired table and comparative dot plots serve different purposes.
records.revision: Replaced the generic sleep example with a school-night/weekend comparison using the same pupils; clarified paired records versus distribution comparison; strengthened sample, measurement, bias and display rationale.
records.remaining: Independent mathematical review of the investigation design and real-child comprehension testing remain pending.

records.title: 立体图形的表面积与体积
records.alignment: CCSS 7.G.B.6 covers composite objects made from polygons, cubes and right prisms; 6.G.A.4 covers nets and surface area.
records.research: Sung et al. provide a specific 3D-representation intervention with 111 fifth-grade students. Lehmann supports flexible face/net strategy choice for simple prisms; Panorkou provides a conceptual account of area and volume reasoning.
coverageAudit: The prior sample included the glued-cube case but omitted a triangular-prism surface-area calculation.
It omitted the L-shaped planter case distinguishing footprint area, soil volume and exterior surface area.
records.revision: Added a 3–4–5 right-triangular prism of length 10 cm: 2×6 + 12×10 = 132 cm². Added an L-shaped 3 m × 3 m footprint with a 1.5 m × 2 m corner removed: base area 6 m², 0.5 m depth gives 3 m³ soil volume; 12 m perimeter gives 6 m² sidewall area, or 12 m² including the base but not the open top. Retained glued-cube result (40 cm³ and 80 cm²).
records.remaining: Independent review must verify right-triangle dimensions, exposed-face accounting and the open-top planter surface-area convention.

records.title: 到平均数的平均距离
records.alignment: CCSS 6.SP.B.5c explicitly names mean absolute deviation; GAISE II Level B defines it as average distance from the mean.
records.research: GAISE II confirms the school-statistics meaning of MAD as mean absolute deviation. NIST distinguishes average absolute deviation (AAD, from the mean) from median absolute deviation (MAD, from the median).
coverageAudit: Interpret the result in the original unit.
Compare two data sets with the same mean to isolate differences in consistency.
records.revision: Spelled out mean absolute deviation to avoid acronym ambiguity; added plant heights 4, 6, 10 and 12 cm (mean 8 cm, MAD 3 cm); added two four-game bowling sets with the same mean 120 and MAD values 8 and 21.
records.remaining: Independent review should verify the convention and each calculation in original units.

records.title: 点图
records.alignment: CCSS 6.SP.B.4 includes dot plots on a number line; the node requires equal spacing, visible gaps, one dot per observation and frequency interpretation.
records.research: Watson and Kelly directly studied Grades 5–10 students interpreting stacked dot plots, including omitted zero-value gaps. NIST documents stacking repeated observations.
coverageAudit: The previous example omitted the full 0–12 scale, four observations at 3, minimum, maximum and mode.
Provide a complete frequency set that can be checked against the stated total of 20 pupils.
records.revision: Added a complete 0–12 frequency sequence for 20 pupils: 3 occurs four times, 5 occurs six times, 7/10/11 are empty, minimum 0, maximum 12 and mode 5.
records.remaining: The dot-plot SVG still requires manual visual checking against the complete scale and stack counts.

records.title: 直方图
records.alignment: CCSS 6.SP.B.4 includes histograms; NIST defines the common equal-bin histogram with frequency counts and distribution features.
records.research: Whitaker and Jacobbe’s LOCUS study documents misunderstandings about reading histograms and distinguishing them from bar graphs in Grades 6–12. NIST supports equal-width bins and frequency-axis definitions.
coverageAudit: Explicitly answer the two required frequency-reading questions.
Require axis labels and justify the difference between continuous intervals and categories.
records.revision: Made interval boundaries explicit and added exact counts: 150≤h<160 contains 6 pupils; below 150 contains 10. Strengthened the task to label height/frequency axes, draw touching equal-width bins and explain the bar-chart distinction.
records.remaining: The histogram SVG still requires manual checking for touching bars, continuous numeric axis, interval boundaries and axis labels.

records.title: 箱线图
records.alignment: CCSS 6.SP.B.4 includes box plots. NIST confirms both min/max-whisker and 1.5-IQR fence-based variants.
records.research: Edwards et al. found a construction/interpretation gap among 259 middle-school students, including difficulty interpreting aggregated data and quartiles. Pfannkuch analyzes the reasoning demands of comparing box-plot distributions.
coverageAudit: State that different raw data sets can share the same five-number summary and box plot.
Distinguish min/max whiskers from 1.5-IQR fence-based box plots.
records.revision: Made the min/max whisker convention explicit, contrasted it with 1.5-IQR fence-based plots, and explained that a five-number summary cannot reveal every cluster, gap or raw value.
records.remaining: The box-plot SVG still requires manual checking; independent review must confirm quartile interpretation and selected whisker convention.

records.title: 分割图形求面积
records.alignment: CCSS 6.G.A.1 explicitly requires composing polygons into rectangles or decomposing them into triangles and other shapes for real-world area problems.
records.research: Lehmann’s Year 8 classroom study (31 participating students) documents decomposition, component-area calculation and recomposition strategies, including errors when students add rather than subtract outside pieces.
coverageAudit: State the perpendicular-diagonal condition; retain the garden task.
records.revision: Added a kite with perpendicular diagonals 8 cm and 6 cm: enclosing rectangle 48 cm² minus four corner triangles totalling 24 cm² gives 24 cm²; direct half-product formula provides a check. Retained trapezoid and 108 m² garden tasks.
records.remaining: The polygon-area SVG still requires manual visual checking; independent review must verify perpendicular diagonals and corner-triangle subtraction.
